title: TensorSpine primitive library unit
description: One logical vocabulary unit of a primitive library base: a primitive definition, a named axis, a precision role, or the base itself. The file path reproduces the unit's identity; a primitive's file name is its version (§8.2). Every enumeration here is the closed vocabulary a consumer may implement in advance (§4.3, O0.6); a unit outside it is refused at load time, never read with a guess (I7). Documentation fields are defined once, in documentation.json, and referenced from the site they document.

argument_path.description: A declared argument, or a field of a record argument, dotted.

expression.description: Closed scalar algebra over literals and resolved arguments (O0.1), conditional included. Every reference resolves to a declared argument.

argument_type.description: The closed set of argument types (O9.4): a scalar, an enum, or a record of such values. There is no opaque type and no reference type: a value the primitive cannot type cannot be refused, and §8.1 requires refusal.

structural.description: The argument decides which slots, ports or states exist, or their shapes; a non-structural argument changes only the computation.
The argument decides which slots, ports or states exist, or their shapes; a non-structural argument changes only the computation.

oneOf.description: The domain of the named input port of this primitive (§5.3).

port_domain.description: A port's indexing domain: `inherit` — the instance's own domain, or the domain of one of its input ports — or a kind, the stream being that of the edge (§5.3).

sharing_rule.description: Whether a slot may be tied to another (§3.4, V15): `exclusive`, or `shareable` with the roles of the slots it may share with.

oneOf.description: The state grows along the stream of the named input port and is frozen once that stream is complete (§5.3).

written_when.description: The condition over the arguments under which the instance writes this state; absent, it always does. An identity instance has exactly one writer among its members (V20): the others read the storage the writer fills.

carried_across.description: The condition over the arguments under which the state survives between the invocations that deliver successive fragments of its stream (§5.3). Declared once per state port.

across_positions.description: The condition over the arguments under which the primitive reads positions of its stream beyond those of the element it produces (O9.5): a convolution reads neighbouring frames, attention every earlier position, a pooler with a reduction the whole sequence; a merge reads only the group its transform declares and does not qualify. Absent, the primitive reads its own element alone. An instance that reads across positions of a fragmented stream must carry a state across that stream's fragments (V18).

oneOf.description: Elementwise: every axis may be partitioned, with no communication.
No meaning-preserving partition exists — a stated fact, never an omission.

communication.description: The logical communication the partition implies — one pattern, or the several a partition admits (`embed`: gather the rows from the shard that owns them, or sum the masked partial lookups of every shard). Which an implementation realises is the manifest's to say.

granularity.description: The number of consecutive coordinates of the target axis a shard keeps whole, an expression over the arguments; absent, one. `attention.dense` partition options its heads by KV group, `heads / kv_heads`, so that a shard's queries find their keys on the shard.

partition.description: One axis along which partition preserves meaning, with the logical communication it implies — several when the partition admits several patterns — and the granularity a shard keeps whole (O7.1). A primitive declares at least one entry: `none` when no graph split preserves meaning. Partition options are declared per instance; their consistency across instances is compilation's (Specification §7, §10.3).

domain_transform.description: How a port's domain relates to the instance's own (§5.3): `merge` — the output carries the input port's stream at the output's kind, one element per `factor` input elements; `align` — the input port carries another domain, the output stays in the instance's domain; `insert` — the input port's elements enter the instance's stream, which the output keeps.

logical_cost.description: Corrections to the derived cost (§4.1, D5). Operations on parameters — two per weight element per element of the output domain, scaled by the activated fraction of a sparse unit — and parameter bytes are derived from the inventory and never declared. A primitive declares only what that rule cannot see: operations on a state, per element or per cached position.

invariants.description: The relations V8 checks on the resolved arguments (§6): each a condition that must hold and a description of what it means. Domains constrain one argument; an invariant relates several.

primitive_definition.description: A primitive definition, or — when it names a `template` — a template primitive (§4.6).

templates.description: Where the templates of this base's template primitives live, relative to the base: one document `<name>/<version>.json` per template version (§4.6). Required when the base carries a template primitive.

name.description: File name of the template, without extension, resolved against the models base.

version.description: The template version pinned by this primitive; the template document must carry the same one (§4.6).

template_primitive.description: A template primitive: its meaning is the family of graphs a template — a parameterized model definition — denotes, one per assignment (§4.6).

sparsity.description: Structured sparsity (§4.5, O6.6): the activatable units of the primitive.

per.description: What the expression is counted per: an element of the instance's output domain, a position held in a state, a sequence, or an invocation (§4.1).

cost_entry.description: One correction to the derived cost, applying where its condition holds; every applying entry contributes (§4.1, O0.5).

unit.description: The activatable unit: the parameter slots that form one unit, and the axis along which units are laid out.

policy.description: What selects the units: an argument (a routing policy), the value on an input port (a token id), or the element itself (its position, its type).

union_per_invocation.description: Upper bound on the union of units an invocation may activate (O6.6).

sparsity_unit.description: One activatable unit (§4.5, O6.6): the slots that form it, the axis it is laid out along, what selects it, how many are activated per element of the output domain, and the bound per invocation. A lookup table is the limiting case: one row per element.

argument_domain_bound.description: An interval endpoint of an argument domain: a value and whether it is inclusive. The value is a scalar literal or a reference to another argument of the same primitive — a bound like `kv_heads <= heads` names `heads`. The referenced argument must be required or defaulted, so it always resolves at a call site (primitive library.primitive_references refuses one that may be absent).

argument_domain.description: A numeric precondition on a primitive argument, checked under V3 after the type at every call site (§4.6): an interval with a lower and/or upper bound, or a finite set of admissible values. Admitted on a cardinality, real or physical argument only; a relation between two arguments (heads a multiple of kv_heads) is an invariant, not a domain.

primitive_invariant.description: A relation the resolved arguments must satisfy for the instance to be admissible — V8 (§6). Evaluated after the types and domains (V3), on the arguments with defaults applied, in the instance's index environment. A condition that reads an argument which may be absent must guard it with a `present` test, as every primitive condition must (§4.3); a condition undecidable for another reason is a refusal, never read as false.

description.description: What the relation means, in words — the text V8 prints when it does not hold.
